items.title: PoC released: CVE-2026-10053
items.description: Reproducible lab for CVE-2026-10053 (GitLab npm package-registry path traversal -> arbitrary file write as git). Vulnerable 19.2.1 vs patched 19.2.2, deterministic oracle.
items.action_detail: Exploitation is plausible and impact is high
items.ai_summary: CVE-2026-10053 is a path traversal vulnerability within the npm package-registry component of GitLab version 19.2.1, leading to arbitrary file write executed in the context of the git user. The vulnerability provides a deterministic exploitation oracle which has a reproducible proof-of-concept available in labs. Successful exploitation enables threat actors to overwrite critical system files. Administrators must upgrade immediately to version 19.2.2 or later to remediate the flaw.
items.why_it_matters: GitLab administrators should update their instances immediately to prevent arbitrary file writes.

items.title: PoC released: CVE-2026-15718
items.description: PoC exploit chain for CVE-2026-15718: SpiderMonkey wasm baseline compiler array.fill missing-sync -> invalid pointer -> addrOf/fakeobj -> arbitrary R/W -> RCE
items.cwe_name: CWE-763 Release of Invalid Pointer or Reference
items.priority_rationale: Public PoC on GitHub · EPSS 0.4% · CVSS 4.3
items.action_detail: Exploitation is plausible and impact is high
items.ai_summary: CVE-2026-15718 is a vulnerability in SpiderMonkey's wasm baseline compiler where an array.fill missing-sync operation creates an invalid pointer. This memory corruption primitive allows attackers to construct addrOf and fakeobj primitives, achieving arbitrary read/write and ultimately remote code execution. A proof-of-concept exploit chain has been released publicly. Mitigation requires applying the official vendor patch for the browser engine.
items.why_it_matters: Browser security teams must apply updates immediately to protect against remote code execution exploits.
